title: What training do truck and bus drivers need for a Driver CPC in the EU?
description: Directive (EU) 2022/2561 explained: 280 hour initial qualification, 35 hours of periodic training every five years, Union code 95 and the 2025 amendments.
shortAnswer: Under Directive (EU) 2022/2561, professional drivers of category C and D vehicles in the EU need a Certificate of Professional Competence (CPC). Initial qualification is either a 280 hour course with a test or a tests only route, with a 140 hour accelerated option. Drivers then complete 35 hours of periodic training every five years at an approved training center, in periods of at least seven hours, with no more than 12 hours of e-learning.
keyTakeaways: The CPC applies to drivers of vehicles needing a C1, C1+E, C, C+E, D1, D1+E, D or D+E license who carry goods or passengers on public roads, subject to the exemptions in Article 2 of Directive (EU) 2022/2561.

Initial qualification by course is 280 hours including at least 20 hours of individual driving; the accelerated qualification is 140 hours with at least 10 hours of individual driving (Annex I, Sections 2 and 3).

Periodic training is 35 hours every five years, delivered by an approved training center in periods of at least seven hours, with e-learning capped at 12 hours and at least one road safety period (Annex I, Section 4).
Completion is shown by the harmonized Union code 95 on the driving license or on a driver qualification card (Article 10).
Directive (EU) 2025/2205 amends Article 5 to allow CPC holders to drive C category trucks from 17 under conditions; Member States must transpose it by November 26, 2028.
jurisdiction: European Union (all Member States; text with EEA relevance)
regulator: European Parliament and Council of the European Union through Directive (EU) 2022/2561, implemented by each Member State's competent authority and its approved training centers
appliesTo: Drivers of goods vehicles in license categories C1, C1+E, C and C+E
Drivers of passenger vehicles in license categories D1, D1+E, D and D+E
Third country nationals employed or used by an undertaking established in a Member State
Road haulage and passenger transport operators, and approved training centers delivering CPC courses

sections.heading: Who needs a Driver CPC under Directive (EU) 2022/2561?

blocks.text: Anyone who drives, for work, a vehicle requiring a C or D category license on public roads in the EU needs a CPC unless an exemption applies. [Directive (EU) 2022/2561](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32022L2561) codified and repealed Directive 2003/59/EC and entered into force on January 12, 2023. Article 1 covers EU nationals and third country nationals employed or used by an undertaking established in a Member State.
Article 2 lists the exemptions. The directive does not apply to drivers of vehicles:

items: with a maximum authorized speed of 45 km/h or less;
used by the armed forces, civil defense, fire service, public order forces and emergency ambulance services when carrying out their tasks;
undergoing road tests for development, repair or maintenance, or new or rebuilt vehicles not yet in service;
used in states of emergency, rescue missions or non-commercial humanitarian transport;
used for non-commercial carriage of passengers or goods;
carrying material, equipment or machinery the driver uses in their work, where driving is not the driver's principal activity.

blocks.text: There are also narrower exemptions for occasional rural own-business transport and for agricultural, horticultural, forestry, farming and fishery undertakings, unless driving is the driver's principal activity or exceeds a distance set in national law. Because each Member State transposes these exemptions, an operator's [training needs analysis](/guides/how-to-conduct-a-training-needs-analysis) should start from the national transposing law, not the directive alone.

Each Member State chooses either a course plus test model or a tests only model under Article 3(1), and may also offer an accelerated qualification. All routes must cover the subject list in Section 1 of Annex I, set at a minimum level comparable to level 2 of the European Qualifications Framework.

blocks.text: Drivers who held a D category license issued no later than September 9, 2008, or a C category license issued no later than September 9, 2009, have acquired rights under Article 4 and are exempt from initial qualification. They are not exempt from periodic training.

sections.heading: How does the 35 hour periodic training cycle work?

blocks.text: Every CPC holder must complete 35 hours of periodic training every five years before their current CPC expires. Section 4 of Annex I requires the hours to be given in periods of at least seven hours, which may be split over two consecutive days, by an approved training center.

items: **First cycle:** under Article 8(2), the first periodic course falls within five years of the initial CPC. Member States may shorten or extend this to align with license expiry, but to no less than three and no more than seven years.
**E-learning cap:** e-learning may not exceed 12 hours, and Member States must require reliable user identification and appropriate means of control.
**Road safety:** at least one of the training periods must cover a road safety related subject.

**Credit for other training:** Member States may count specific training required by other EU law, such as dangerous goods training under Directive 2008/68/EC, for up to one seven hour period, or two periods where dangerous goods training is the only other training counted.
**Returning drivers:** a driver who has stopped driving professionally and whose CPC has lapsed must complete a periodic course before resuming (Article 8(4)).

blocks.text: Article 7 states the purpose: periodic training lets CPC holders "update the knowledge which is essential for their work, with specific emphasis on road safety, health and safety at work, and the reduction of the environmental impact of driving." It should take account of legal and technological change and, as far as possible, the individual driver's training needs, including repeat training where remedial work is shown to be needed. A five year cycle of identical modules does not meet that intent.

sections.heading: Which subjects must CPC training cover?

blocks.text: Section 1 of Annex I lists three subject groups, with some objectives specific to goods or passenger licenses. Periodic training revises and expands on a selection of them rather than repeating all of them.

items: **Advanced training in rational driving based on safety regulations:** transmission and braking systems, driver assistance systems such as AEBS and ESP, fuel optimization, anticipating traffic risks and adverse weather, and load securing (goods) or passenger comfort and safety (passengers).

**Application of regulations:** driving and rest time rules under Regulation (EC) No 561/2006, tachograph use under Regulation (EU) No 165/2014, and the rules governing carriage of goods or passengers.

**Health, road and environmental safety, service and logistics:** accident risks, preventing criminality and trafficking in illegal immigrants, ergonomics, the effects of alcohol, drugs, fatigue and stress, emergency response and first aid, and company image.

blocks.title: Design implication
blocks.text: Because periodic training must include at least one road safety period and should reflect each driver's needs, a training plan that links each driver's incident, telematics and tachograph findings to the Section 1 objectives is easier to defend than a fixed catalog chosen by the training center.

sections.heading: How is completion proved and recorded?

blocks.text: Completion is proved by the harmonized Union code 95 marked next to the relevant categories on the driving license or on a driver qualification card. Under Article 10, the card follows the EU model in Annex II and is mutually recognized between Member States.

Third country goods drivers may instead prove their qualification with a driver attestation under Regulation (EC) No 1072/2009 bearing code 95. Article 11 requires Member States to exchange information on CPCs issued or withdrawn through an electronic enforcement network. Operators are not given a separate record keeping rule in the directive, so employer obligations on retention come from national law. For setting retention periods, see [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records).

sections.heading: What is changing for Driver CPC rules?

blocks.text: Directive (EU) 2025/2205 on driving licences, adopted on October 22, 2025, amends Article 5 of Directive (EU) 2022/2561. As at November 2026 the amendment has been adopted but is not yet required to be applied in national law.

items: A new Article 5(2)(c) allows drivers from age 17 to drive C1, C1E or C vehicles if they hold the relevant CPC, under the conditions in Article 17(2) and (3) of [Directive (EU) 2025/2205](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32025L2205).

A replaced Article 5(3) lets passenger drivers drive D and D+E vehicles from 21 with either type of CPC, and allows Member States to monitor CPC holders under 23. Road safety periodic training required for those drivers counts toward the 35 hours.
Member States must adopt transposing measures by November 26, 2028 and apply them generally from November 26, 2029, with measures for Article 17 applying from November 26, 2028.

blocks.text: The 35 hour, five year periodic training requirement in Annex I is not changed by these amendments. For handling such updates, see [how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry turns each Annex I objective into a defined knowledge point with assessment items before any course content is written, so an operator can see which objectives a driver covered in each five year cycle and which remain open. That supports the directive's expectation that periodic training reflects individual driver needs rather than repeating the same modules.

faqs.q: Can all 35 hours of Driver CPC periodic training be done online?
faqs.a: No. Section 4 of Annex I to Directive (EU) 2022/2561 caps e-learning at 12 hours per five year cycle and requires reliable user identification and controls. The remaining hours must be delivered by an approved training center as classroom teaching, practical training or, where available, simulator training.

faqs.q: Does a driver who changes employer need to repeat periodic training?
faqs.a: No. Article 7 states that if a driver moves to another undertaking, periodic training already undergone shall be taken into account. The new employer should still obtain proof of the completed hours and check the code 95 expiry date.

faqs.q: Do drivers with acquired rights need periodic training?
faqs.a: Yes. Article 4 exempts drivers whose D license was issued by September 9, 2008 or whose C license was issued by September 9, 2009 from initial qualification only. Article 8(4) confirms that drivers with acquired rights must complete periodic training to keep driving professionally.

faqs.q: Can a dangerous goods course count toward the 35 hours?
faqs.a: It can if the Member State allows it. Annex I lets Member States count specific training required under other EU law, including ADR training under Directive 2008/68/EC, for up to one seven hour period, or two periods if dangerous goods training is the only other training counted.

faqs.q: Where must a driver complete periodic training?
faqs.a: Article 9 requires periodic training in the Member State where the driver has their normal residence or the Member State where they work. Initial qualification is taken in the Member State of normal residence, or for third country nationals where the undertaking is established or the work permit was issued.

factCheck.claim: Directive applies to drivers of vehicles needing C1, C1+E, C, C+E, D1, D1+E, D or D+E licenses, including third country nationals employed by EU undertakings; Article 2 exemptions include vehicles up to 45 km/h, emergency services, non-commercial carriage and equipment carriage where driving is not the principal activity

Initial qualification by course is 280 hours with at least 20 hours individual driving (up to 8 on simulator or special terrain); tests only route has a theory test of at least 4 hours, a 90 minute driving test and a 30 minute practical test; accelerated qualification is 140 hours with 10 hours driving; 70 and 35 hours for Article 5(5) drivers

Periodic training is 35 hours every five years in periods of at least seven hours, e-learning maximum 12 hours, at least one road safety period, other EU training may count for one period or two for dangerous goods
First periodic course within five years of CPC issue, adjustable to between three and seven years; drivers returning after a lapse must complete periodic training (Article 8)
Acquired rights for D licenses issued no later than 9 September 2008 and C licenses issued no later than 9 September 2009 (Article 4)
Union code 95 marked on the driving license or driver qualification card, mutually recognized (Article 10); minimum level comparable to EQF level 2 (Annex I Section 1)
Directive (EU) 2022/2561 entered into force on 12 January 2023 and is modified by Directive (EU) 2025/2205 (Article 5(2)(c) added and Article 5(3) replaced)

Directive (EU) 2025/2205 of 22 October 2025 allows CPC holders to drive C1, C1E or C from 17 under Article 17 conditions; D and D+E from 21 with either CPC; under 23 road safety periodic training counts toward 35 hours; transposition by 26 November 2028, application from 26 November 2029, Article 17 from 26 November 2028
